old-town-lipscani.name: Old Town: Lipscani, Cărturești Carusel, Hanul lui Manuc & Curtea Veche
old-town-lipscani.name_ro: Centrul Vechi: Lipscani, Cărturești Carusel, Hanul lui Manuc, Curtea Veche
old-town-lipscani.blurb: The pedestrian medieval core: guild-named lanes, the white "carousel" bookshop, the 1808 caravanserai and Vlad the Impaler's princely court.

footprint.note: ~320 m E-W x 380 m N-S between Str. Smârdan (W), Bd. I. C. Brătianu (E), Str. Lipscani/Gabroveni (N) and Str. Franceză / Piața Unirii edge (S). All pedestrian streets (maxspeed 20, vehicles only for deliveries before 10:00).

structures.name: Cărturești Carusel (Lipscani 55)
structures.osm: way/658009149 (building polygon containing shop node/3355049764; 27.4 x 13.4 m, ~354 m², long axis ~N-S, narrow front on Lipscani)

dims.note: six levels incl. top-floor bistro; atrium with white undulating balconies and spiral/curving stair

structures.history: Built 1860, bought in the early 1900s by the Chrissoveloni bankers (bank HQ), later a communist general store, decayed; 5-year rehabilitation, opened as bookshop in 2015 (design by Square One architects).

facade.style: Eclectic 19th-century bank/shop palace, 4 storeys + attic on the street; cream stucco with pilasters, tall ground-floor arched shop windows with dark frames

interior.features: brilliant white curved balustrades on every level stacked like a carousel around a tall atrium, glass skylight, white columns with simple capitals, black-and-white checkered/stone floor at ground level, wooden bookshelves (#B48A5A) and thousands of books (>10,000 titles), warm pendant lights; bistro on the top floor

signage: CĂRTUREȘTI CARUSEL (brass/black lettering above the entrance)

structures.name: Hanul lui Manuc (Manuc's Inn), Str. Franceză 62-64

dims.note: closed quadrangle around a large courtyard; OSM building:colour=white, material=brick, roof brown

facade.galleries: continuous wooden balconies (gallery/foișor) on the upper floor all round the courtyard, dark-stained wood posts and balustrades (#5A3A22); over the street gate an enclosed, glazed dark-timber gallery projects
facade.roof: hipped roof with a very deep overhanging eave on exposed dark rafters (#2A2420), dark brown/grey tiles
facade.street_facade: 2 storeys of whitewashed walls (#E6E7E7) articulated by flat pilasters with small carved stucco capitals, small 6-pane casement windows in brown frames (#5C3B26), carved stucco grille vents, rough stone plinth; arched carriage gateway with the words HANUL MANUC in black letters on the arch (flower garland in spring) and a clock visible in the courtyard
facade.ground_floor: arched arcade openings in the courtyard

structures.courtyard: paved courtyard with restaurant terrace tables, wooden well/pergola, vine/trees, umbrellas
signage: HANU' LUI MANUC RESTAURANT® (gold serif letters on a black rounded-corner plaque left of the gate)
HANUL MANUC (black letters on the gate arch)

structures.name: Curtea Veche - Palatul Voievodal (Old Princely Court ruins)

dims.note: excavated brick vaults and walls, partly roofed museum

facade.material: old orange-red brick and river stone, low ruined walls

structures.extras: Bronze bust of Vlad III Țepeș (Dracula) on a stone pedestal at the ruins (tourist magnet)

structures.name: Biserica Curtea Veche (Buna Vestire), Str. Franceză 33
structures.note: Built by Mircea Ciobanul in 1559; oldest religious building in Bucharest maintained in its original aspect; alternating bands of red brick and white plaster, round brick-ribbed tower drum, grey metal roof

structures.name: Strada Lipscani
structures.note: Named after Leipzig (Lipsca) traders; 2-4 storey 19th-c eclectic shop houses with ornate stucco, cast-iron balconies, ground-floor bars/shops, terrace tables in summer.

ground.area: pedestrian streets (Lipscani, Franceză, Șelari, Smârdan, Gabroveni)
ground.surface: small grey granite cobbles/setts (~10 cm) laid in loose rows across the whole street width, no kerbs (shared surface), occasional larger slab bands and cast-iron manhole covers (OSM: sett / paving_stones / paved)

vegetation.summary: Dense historic core with few trees: 134 OSM trees in the wider footprint (mostly around Curtea Veche, Manuc courtyard and the Brătianu edge); small grass beds at the ruins; vines and potted plants on terraces.

street_furniture: terrace pergolas with green/cream canvas awnings over wooden chairs and cushioned rattan sofas, potted bamboo screens, string lights (photo Lipscani looking east)
black cast-iron historic-style street lamps ~4.5 m with lantern heads, some double-headed; wall-bracket lanterns
A-frame chalkboard/printed boards (e.g. "CIGARETTES WINES TOBACCO LIQUORS CIGARS"), Coca-Cola branded menu stands, ATM signs
wrought-iron balconies, AC units and overhead cables on façades
old-town-lipscani.lighting: Night is peak time: warm lantern lamps, illuminated bar signs, string lights across lanes, Carusel atrium glowing white through the arched windows.
old-town-lipscani.backdrop: East: the tall grey office block with the NTT DATA rooftop sign visible at the end of Lipscani (on Bd. I. C. Brătianu); south-east: Piața Unirii; north: Hanul Gabroveni (Salvador Dali Universe exhibition 2024), National Bank palace; west: Stavropoleos spot.

crowd.typical: Busiest place in the city: daytime tour groups and couples; evenings/weekends packed with young locals and stag/hen groups; terrace waiters inviting passers-by. Old Town was the most-searched attraction by foreigners (Visit Bucharest 2022) and top-3 in 2024.

ambient_sounds: bar music spilling out (pop/house), occasional lăutari violin/accordion

plaques.title: Lipscani = Leipzig
plaques.text: Lipscani is named after Leipzig (Lipsca): traders here sold goods brought from the West.

plaques.title: Guild streets
plaques.text: Neighbouring streets keep the old guild names: Blănari (furriers), Șelari (saddlers).

plaques.title: Manuc's Inn (1808)
plaques.text: Manuc's Inn was built in 1808 by the Armenian merchant Manuc Bei; talks for the 1812 Treaty of Bucharest were held here.

plaques.title: Curtea Veche, 1459
plaques.text: Curtea Veche: Vlad III (Dracula) dated a document from his "fortress of Bucharest" on 20 September 1459.

plaques.title: Curtea Veche church
plaques.text: The Curtea Veche church (1559) is the oldest church in Bucharest kept in its original form.

plaques.title: Cărturești Carusel
plaques.text: Cărturești Carusel: an 1860 bank building, restored and reopened as a 6-floor bookshop in 2015. "Cărturești" is the chain's name, not "light".

interaction.title: Carousel climb & Dracula hunt
interaction.desc: Enter Cărturești Carusel and climb the white balconies to the top-floor bistro to unlock the atrium postcard; outside, find Vlad the Impaler's bust at Curtea Veche while vendors try to sell you "Dracula" magnets (say "Nu, mersi").
interaction.true_to_place: Carusel is the most photographed interior in Bucharest; Vlad III really founded the princely court.

photo_angle.note: Inside Carusel from the 2nd-floor balcony at the entrance side looking into the atrium and up at the stacked white balconies. Exterior alt: Str. Franceză at [44.43010,26.10180] heading 80 deg looking at Manuc's Inn gate at dusk.

seasonal_time_of_day: Summer nights: terraces full until 02:00 (Manuc Fri-Sa 10-02, OSM).
Winter: terrace heaters, mulled wine, Christmas lights strung across lanes.
Mornings: delivery vans, cleaning trucks, almost empty.
old-town-lipscani.copyright_note: Carusel interior (2015 redesign) is a recent copyrighted work and Romania has no freedom of panorama: use interior photos as modelling reference only.

structures.name: Biserica Mănăstirii Stavropoleos (1724)

dims.note: OSM footprint; small single-nave church with a polygonal altar apse and a single tower/dome over the nave

facade.portico: open porch (pridvor) of slender carved stone columns (spiral/foliate shafts, carved capitals) carrying trefoil (three-lobed) arches, low stone parapet between columns
facade.walls: lower register: cream stone ashlar with blind trefoil arcades and a small barred window; middle frieze: band of round medallions with painted saints on a dark blue-grey ground framed by red-brown and ochre painted bands; carved stone cornice
facade.roof: terracotta clay-tile roof with a deep overhang on carved wooden brackets; octagonal cream drum (tower) with small rectangular windows under a red-tile conical/bell cap and an iron cross; separate red-tile domed roofs on the Ion Mincu courtyard building next door

structures.enclosure: low cream stone wall with square stone piers topped by urn finials and black wrought-iron grille panels (ring/quatrefoil pattern) around the church; black iron gate
structures.courtyard: Cloister-like courtyard (Ion Mincu building, early 20th c.) with arcades and a lapidarium of carved stone crosses and tombstones; flowers and climbing vines

structures.name: Caru' cu Bere (Str. Stavropoleos 5)
structures.history: Brewery opened 1879; restaurant opened 1899 in a Gothic-Revival building by architect Siegfried Kofczinski; historic monument B-II-m-B-19728; ~2,500 customers a day in 2014, 36% foreigners.

facade.details: pointed-arch windows with stone tracery, small corner turret, stained-glass, wrought-iron lanterns, carved wooden doors

structures.interior: 7 m high beer hall, Gothic columns, painted stucco vaults, carved oak staircases, Art Nouveau stained glass and murals

structures.name: Palatul CEC (Calea Victoriei 13)

dims.note: central glass-and-metal dome + four Renaissance corner domes

facade.details: entrance: semicircular arch on two pairs of composite columns; corner pavilions with pediments and coats of arms; central glazed dome with metal ribs

signage: CASA DE DEPUNERI, CONSEMNAȚIUNI ȘI ECONOMIE (inscription)

structures.name: Muzeul Național de Istorie a României (former Post Palace), Calea Victoriei 12

facade.details: portico of 10 Doric columns on a high base reached by 12 steps spanning the façade; allegorical sculpture

structures.extras: On the steps: bronze statue of Emperor Trajan (sculptor Vasile Gorduz, 2012) - naked emperor holding a Dacian wolf, much-discussed and photographed

ground.surface: small grey granite setts laid in overlapping fan/arc (segmental) pattern, framed by bands of large light granite slabs (photo: Biserica Stavropoleos B-II-m-A-19464)
asphalt, 2 lanes + bike lane, wide sidewalks of grey pavers
stone slabs and cobbles, grass strips

vegetation.summary: 108 OSM trees in footprint: notably 61 Prunus persica (ornamental) and Fagus, Tilia platyphyllos, Abies alba, Aesculus hippocastanum; courtyard of Stavropoleos has flowers, roses and climbing vines.

street_furniture: flagpoles on CEC and the museum (10 OSM flagpoles)
stavropoleos-cec.lighting: CEC and history museum floodlit warm; Caru' cu Bere glowing interior and lanterns; church courtyard dim.
stavropoleos-cec.backdrop: Calea Victoriei continues north towards Palatul Telefoanelor and Cercul Militar (eclectic 4-6 storey façades); Dâmbovița embankment and Splaiul Independenței traffic to the south; Old Town lanes (Lipscani spot) to the east; National Bank of Romania palace on Str. Lipscani to the north-east.

crowd.typical: Queue outside Caru' cu Bere at lunch/dinner, tourists photographing Stavropoleos portico, worshippers (lighting candles in the candle house), museum visitors posing with Trajan.

ambient_sounds: Byzantine chant from the church (choir founded 1994) on service times
restaurant bustle and folk music from Caru' cu Bere

plaques.title: Stavropoleos (1724)
plaques.text: Stavropoleos church was built in 1724 by the Greek monk Ioanikie Stratonikeas; the name means "City of the Cross".

plaques.title: Byzantine chant
plaques.text: Its choir sings neo-Byzantine chant, rare in Romania today, and the library holds Romania's largest Byzantine music collection.

plaques.title: Caru' cu Bere
plaques.text: Caru' cu Bere began as a brewery in 1879; the neo-Gothic beer hall opened in 1899.

plaques.title: CEC Palace
plaques.text: The CEC Palace foundation stone was laid on 8 June 1897 in the presence of King Carol I; architect Paul Gottereau.

plaques.title: National History Museum
plaques.text: The History Museum, in the former Post Palace, holds a full plaster cast of Trajan's Column and the Romanian Crown Jewels.

interaction.title: Trajan's pose
interaction.desc: Strike the same pose as the bronze naked Trajan with the Dacian wolf on the museum steps for a photo challenge; then light a candle in the Stavropoleos candle house (quiet zone: running is slowed to walking in the courtyard).
interaction.true_to_place: The Trajan statue is the most joked-about statue in the city; candle-lighting is what locals actually do here.

culture.note: "Bună ziua" (good day) is the safe greeting with strangers; "Salut"/"Hey" among young people. Use "dumneavoastră" (formal you) with older people; elderly men may still say "Sărut mâna" (I kiss your hand) to women as an old-fashioned courtesy. Thank you = "Mulțumesc" or the very common French loan "Mersi".
Bună dimineața (morning), Bună ziua (day), Bună seara (evening); Noapte bună only when parting at night. Pick by the scene clock.

Romanian is a Romance language; young educated people usually speak good English, older educated people often French/Italian/Spanish. Italians/Spanish tourists often half-understand Romanian signs. So bubbles: Romanian for locals with English translation; tourists speak their own language.

Foreign visitors to Bucharest searching online in 2024 came mostly from UK, US, Germany, Bulgaria, Italy, Greece, Israel, Netherlands and France; British searched for Therme, Americans for "Wednesday" filming locations and Romanian food, Bulgarians for Christmas markets/concerts. Use these origins for tourist personas.
Never assume a car will stop at a crosswalk; drivers can be inconsiderate. Locals joke and grumble about traffic, honking, sidewalk parking and buses; keep it good-humoured, never aggressive.

Typical words: mici/mititei (grilled minced-meat rolls), ciorbă de burtă (tripe soup), sarmale (cabbage rolls), papanași (doughnuts with sour cream and jam), covrigi (pretzels sold from street windows). Caru' cu Bere, Berăria H and Hanu' lui Manuc were the most-searched restaurants by foreign tourists in 2024.

Orthodox churches (Stavropoleos, Patriarchal/National Cathedral): people cross themselves when passing, speak quietly, women often cover their heads, shoulders/knees covered; avoid flash and ask before photographing services. Nuns/priests are greeted with "Bună ziua" or "Doamne-ajută" (God help); do not script jokes about clergy.
culture.source: general Orthodox etiquette (no single source fetched from this environment - verify with church staff signage)

culture.note: Romanians are hospitable and insist when offering something ("no" is often treated as politeness and the offer repeated) - vendors/elders can repeat an offer once before accepting a refusal. Respect for the elderly is valued; older men may kiss a lady's hand; handshakes are standard.

Vlad the Impaler is seen by many Romanians as a national hero; some are offended when he is equated with Count Dracula - so locals in bubbles push back ("Vlad Țepeș was one of ours, not a vampire!"). Opinions on Ceaușescu vary; some older people speak of him positively - an elder persona may be nostalgic, others critical; never caricature either.
Avoid lines implying Romanian is Slavic or that Romania was part of the USSR; never confuse Romanians with Roma people.
Unsolicited offers of help/taxis near tourist areas can be scams; locals recommend Bolt/Uber. A vendor/tout persona may push magnets or taxis politely; the player can just walk away.

Communism and Ceaușescu are top tourist interests ("Communism and communist buildings remain at the top of searches"). Locals talk about it with dark irony (e.g. calling the Memorial of Rebirth "the impaled potato"), but lines must stay factual and avoid mocking victims of 1989 (around 1,500 died).

Do not use ethnic jokes (in particular about Roma people) or Dracula/vampire clichés aimed at locals; Dracula appears only as souvenir-vendor patter and as a historical fact (Vlad III built the Old Princely Court).

1 March: mărțișor (red-and-white string trinkets) sold everywhere and given to women; December: "Crăciun fericit!" and the Christmas market in Piața Constituției; winter: "Ce ger!" (what frost); summer heatwaves: "caniculă" (summers often exceed 30 °C).
